* Overview

This file enumerates every one of the 86 routable page types (plus one
auxiliary =subType= companion, 87 array entries total) recognised by
=ShowAllEntityData.user.js=, as declared in the =pageDefinitions= array
(=ShowAllEntityData.user.js:12073-14907= as of this sync — re-grep
=const pageDefinitions = [= rather than trust this range, it drifts
as the script grows) and gated by the four
=// @include= regexes in the userscript header. For each page type it gives
a real, clickable MusicBrainz URL (using live MBIDs looked up via the
MusicBrainz web service), the script's =tableMode=, the button(s) that
trigger it, and a plain-language summary of which script features actually
fire (column extractors, injected columns, collapsible cells, CAA/EAA
artwork, sticky columns, etc.).

Wherever the page type is tied to a specific entity, the entity is
Bruce Springsteen or something directly connected to him (his catalogue,
Columbia Records, The Stone Pony, New Jersey, ...). A handful of page types
are inherently global/editor-scoped (reports, elections, tag lookup,
genres, CD stubs, ISRC lookup, user-owned collections) and use real but
not-Springsteen-specific MusicBrainz identifiers instead — noted inline.
Two entries (=collections-releases= and every =user-*= page type) need an
identifier that belongs to a specific editor/collection; the editor
username =vzell= is used throughout since it is a real, publicly viewable
MusicBrainz account, but a real collection MBID could not be found by
search and is left as a =<collection-mbid>= placeholder.

* Coverage clusters & representatives

Most of the 86 page types above are structural near-duplicates of a
smaller number of shapes (same =tableMode=/feature pipeline, different
entity kind or column names). This section names those clusters, picks
1-2 representatives per cluster for the =tests/snapshots/= regression
harness (rather than one capture per type), and tracks capture status.
No new captures happened in this pass — see the =add-snapshot-pagetype=
skill for turning a =planned= row into a =captured= one.

** Identifier selection criteria

1. Default to Bruce Springsteen or a directly-connected entity — reuse an
   existing ~Identifier legend~ abbreviation before minting a new one.
   Only global/admin pages with no natural entity anchor (reports,
   elections, CD stubs, ISRC lookup, tag lookup) keep a non-Springsteen
   identifier, matching this doc's existing practice.
2. Prefer the smallest-catalog qualifying identifier (ideally a single
   native MB page) unless the representative's whole point is exercising
   pagination, in which case use the minimum page count that still
   triggers it — 2 native pages (see =RG_GREET='s existing use in
   =tests/live/release-group-paginated-fetch.spec.js= for the precedent).
3. Row count risk is NOT uniform across page shapes anchored on the same
   identifier: an aggregate/summary list (tags, aliases, ratings count)
   stays tiny regardless of how prolific the anchor entity is, but a
   per-item listing (releases, recordings, relationships) scales with the
   anchor's real catalog. =ARTIST= (Bruce Springsteen, 2000+ release
   groups) and =INSTR_GT= ("Guitar", used on presumably thousands of
   recordings) are both already in the legend for good reasons (they're
   real, well-documented Springsteen/generic-instrument identifiers) but
   are a poor fit for the *listing*-shaped representatives flagged below —
   pick a smaller substitute for those specific rows at capture time
   (a session musician, a specific instrument like "lap steel guitar",
   etc.), not for the aggregate-shaped rows that reuse the same
   abbreviation safely.
